ĭn-ausus , a, um, adj.,
I.not ventured, unattempted (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): “ne quid inausum Aut intractatum scelerisve dolive fuisset,” Verg. A. 8, 205 : “nefas,” Val. Fl. 1, 807 : “quid enim per hosce dies inausum intemeratumve vobis?” Tac. A. 1, 42 : “sciat animus nihil inausum esse fortunae,” Sen. Ep. 91
med.—Plur. as subst.: ĭn-ausa , ōrum, n., unattempted things, deeds beyond daring: “quae inausa audeat,” Sen. Thyest. 20 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
